jobs.title: Senior Manager, Corporate Strategy
jobs.description:
Founded in 1986, Westlake Corporation (NYSE: WLK) is a Fortune 500 global diversified industrial company that manufactures and supplies essential products that enhance the daily lives of people around the globe. Our products are used in housing and infrastructure, packaging and healthcare, and automotive and consumer goods.

SUMMARY
As Senior Manager – Corporate Strategy you will play a crucial role in regularly partnering and engaging with executive leadership team, business unit leadership and other stakeholders to shape strategic direction, drive portfolio-level initiatives, navigate complex business environments and build disciplined strategy execution capabilities across the organization.
With approximately 8+ of relevant experience, the Senior Manager – Corporate Strategy brings deep expertise in corporate and business-unit strategy, operating model design, and the ability to effectively guide matrixed project teams to deliver desired results.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
May include, but are not limited to, the following:
- Strategic business planning and analysis
- Serve as a key thought partner in identifying, evaluating, and prioritizing new strategic business opportunities, with frequent exposure to and interaction with executive leadership.

- Develop and deliver insightful market, competitive, and financial analyses to inform short- and long-term strategic planning; translate findings into clear recommendations for senior leadership.

- Develop robust business cases and financial models, including scenario analysis and forecasts, evaluate strategic options, quantify value creation, and support investment decisions.

- Monitor performance of strategic initiatives against targets; track KPIs, identify risks and variances, and recommend corrective actions to ensure expected outcomes are achieved.

- Market entry, business development, and corporate development
- Systematically scan, identify, and assess organic and inorganic growth opportunities by business, geography, and region, ensuring alignment with the enterprise strategic plan and portfolio priorities.

- Conduct rigorous, fact-based analysis of market trends, customer requirements, competitive dynamics, regulatory developments, technology advancements, and new product innovations.

- Support corporate development efforts including target screening, due diligence, deal structuring, partnerships, and post-merger integration.

- Business transformation
- Partner with business leaders and Project Managers to scope, design, and execute large-scale transformation initiatives that align with the strategic plan and deliver measurable business outcomes.

- Apply disciplined project and program management practices to develop charters, detailed project plans, timelines, resource plans, and risk/issue logs; track progress against milestones and escalate concerns as needed.

- Develop compelling written communications (white-papers, PowerPoint) to gain alignment and approval from C-suite

EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS
- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, Finance, Engineering, or related field required.

- Advanced degree (MBA or related) preferred but not required.

- 8+ years of relevant professional experience, with a significant portion in management consulting, corporate strategy, or strategic planning.

- Strong executive presence and communication skills—able to distill complex ideas into concise, compelling narratives and present recommendations in an executive setting.

- Demonstrated track record leading complex, multi-stakeholder strategy projects from conception through execution, manage multiple priorities, and deliver high-quality work under tight timelines.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit; stand; walk; use hands to touch, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stoop, kneel, or crouch. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 5 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 15 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus. Significant digital dexterity, e.g. using computer keyboard is required. Use of oral communication to perform work is required.

WORK ENVIRONMENT
The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate as normally based in an open office concept. Some of the work may be required in the operating units which can require usage of required PPE including safety glasses, hearing protection, etc. May also result in exposure to outside elements and may require usage of stairs and elevators.

Westlake offers you the potential to enrich your work life and career experience in an entrepreneurial environment. We work together to enhance peoples lives through our products and presence in the communities in which we operate.

jobs.title: Sr. Manager - Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
SUMMARY
Reporting directly to the Roofing & Stone Division Controller, this role serves as a key finance business partner to the leadership team. This role will provide strategic financial insights, drive planning & forecasting processes, and support profitable growth across our manufacturing operations.

ACCOUNTING DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
May include, but are not limited to, the following:
- Lead the annual budgeting, monthly forecasting, strategic planning, and financial consolidation processes across the division.

- Develop, maintain, and communicate budgets, forecasts, financial reports, operational analyses, and executive-level presentation packages

- Responsible for all SGA related reporting, forecast, budget and variance analysis

- Prepare and manage monthly, quarterly, and annual business reviews, including sales reviews, plants’ reviews, Division business review and corporate presentations.

- Monitor financial performance against budget, forecast, and prior-year results, identifying key drivers, risks, and opportunities.

- Communicate consolidated financial and operational performance trends using relevant metrics and KPIs, providing actionable recommendations to leadership.

- Partner closely with Commercial Operations to provide analytical support on sales performance, pricing strategies, margins, and profitability initiatives.

- Assess product, customer, and channel profitability and provide recommendations to commercial leadership to support growth and margin expansion.

- Manage all sales related commission processes.

- Collaborate with Pricing team on rebate program management.

- Develop EBITDA bridges, variance analyses, financial commentaries, and management insights explaining results against budget, forecast, and prior-year performance.

- Support strategic initiatives by developing business cases, financial models, investment analyses, and recommendations for leadership decision-making.

- Monitor capital spending, forecast capital requirements, evaluate project paybacks, and ensure alignment with business objectives.

- Develop and enhance financial models, dashboards, and reporting tools utilizing advanced analytics and visualization technologies.

- Drive continuous improvement initiatives to increase forecasting accuracy, reporting efficiency, and analytical capabilities.

- Lead, coach, and develop the FP&A team, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and professional growth.

- Support and enforce compliance with SOX requirements, internal controls, and company policies and procedures.

- Perform additional duties and special projects as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS, EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE
- B.S. in Finance or Accounting or a related field is required.

- An advanced degree in Finance/Accounting and/or certification (CPA, CMA, or MBA) is highly preferred

- Minimum 10 years of experience in FP&A with solid track record in a manufacturing environment, with a deep understanding of operational drivers is required.

- Costing Accounting background preferred.

- Prior people management experience is required.

- Advanced excel skills including complex financial modeling and data analysis

- Expert using HFM, Onstream or BPC

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with experience in operational analysis and variance reporting.

- Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills.

- SAP, JDE and PBI experience is a plus.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Treasury Operations
jobs.description:
SUMMARY
The Associate Director, Treasury Operations is responsible for leading day‑to‑day global cash management, banking operations, foreign exchange and treasury control activities. This role ensures adequate liquidity, efficient use of cash, effective management of bank relationships, and compliance with corporate Delegation of Authority (DOA) and treasury policies across Westlake. The position partners closely with Finance, Accounting, Tax, Legal, and business units to support funding, risk management, and capital markets activities

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
- Oversee daily cash positioning, including cash concentration, funding, and investing in accordance with approved guidelines and DOA.
- Owns short‑term 13 week cash flow forecasting processes and ensure alignment with FP&A, Accounting, and business units.
- Optimize use of bank credit lines, including revolver draws/repayments and debt service execution within delegated authority.
- Monitor global cash balances and support strategies to repatriate or redeploy cash efficiently, in coordination with Tax and Treasury leadership.
- Own and continuously improve core treasury processes (cash management, payments, intercompany funding, bank fee analysis, etc.).
- Partner with FP&A, Accounting, Tax, Legal, and Corporate Credit to align treasury operations with broader capital structure, working capital, and risk management strategies
- Ensure accurate and timely recording of treasury transactions in the general ledger and sub systems.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related field required.
- Advanced degree (MBA or related) and/or professional designation (CTP, CFA, CPA) preferred.
- 8–10+ years of progressive experience in treasury, corporate finance, or banking; experience in a multinational industrial, chemicals, or manufacturing environment preferred.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit; stand; walk; use hands to touch, handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stoop, kneel or crouch. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and the ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT
The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate, as the role is primarily based in an office setting (e.g., Westlake Corporate offices in Houston 5, 6). Some travel may be required for investor conferences, roadshows, plant/site tours with investors and internal meetings. Travel is typically up to 15–25%, including domestic and international air and automobile travel.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
The Senior Director, FP&A leads corporate financial planning and analysis activities across Westlake, with responsibility for enterprise-level FP&A deliverables and for partnering with segment and business unit finance teams (e.g., Performance & Essential Materials and Housing & Infrastructure Products segments). The incumbent serves as a key strategic finance leader and business partner to executive leadership, shaping Westlake’s financial plans in support of its long-term strategy and capital deployment priorities.

This role is accountable for driving an integrated, disciplined budgeting and target-setting process across the enterprise. The Senior Director, FP&A works closely with segment and business unit leaders to translate strategic and operational plans into clear financial targets, challenge underlying assumptions, and establish robust cost and productivity objectives. Through enhanced budget frameworks, standardized methodologies, and transparent performance dashboards, the incumbent increases ownership and accountability for results, improves cost visibility and accountability, and enables proactive cost management and margin optimization.

The Senior Director, FP&A also leads the development and continuous improvement of Westlake’s enterprise forecasting capabilities. This includes designing and refining driver-based forecasting models, coordinating regular forecast cycles with segment and business unit finance teams, identifying and implementing technological solutions to improve efficiency and effectiveness in the FP&A process, and implementing scenario and sensitivity analyses to assess the impact of market conditions, commodity price movements, and operational initiatives on earnings and cash flow. The incumbent plays a central role in supporting more accurate, insight-driven earnings guidance by ensuring forecasts are analytically rigorous, aligned with business realities, and effectively synthesized for the Executive Management team and other key stakeholders. Strong communication and collaboration skills are necessary.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
- Lead the preparation, and presentation when required, of financial reports, executive‑level presentations, and related analysis for Senior Management and the Board of Directors for periodic Board meetings, monthly and quarterly business reviews, and other senior leadership forums.
- Work across senior financial leadership including the Segment CFOs and Business Unit Finance Directors to standardize processes, financial information, and associated reporting and KPI metrics to ensure a coherent view of performance analytics. performance drivers. and insight.
- Develop and maintain a robust KPI framework and executive dashboards that tightly link operational metrics to financial outcomes and strategic objectives.
- Synthesize complex financial, operational, and market information into clear insights and recommendations supporting corporate strategy and capital allocation decisions.
- Support the CFO, CEO, and other members of the executive team in capital allocation decisions, including evaluation and prioritization of capital projects, strategic investments and productivity initiatives.
- Serve as a primary FP&A contact for the CEO, CFO, CAO, Treasurer and segment leadership on planning, forecasting and performance topics.
- Identify, assess and implement technological tools to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the FP&A function in collaboration with other stakeholders such as the Sr. Director of Business Transformation, CAO, and Segment CFOs.  Identify and utilize Artificial Intelligence and other digital tools in value-added ways.
- Lead the development of short- and long-range strategic plans at the corporate level, integrating inputs from segments and businesses and reflecting market, macroeconomic, and industry specific dynamics.
- Own and consolidate the Annual Operating Plan and Capital Plan across Westlake.
- Lead recurring forecasting processes, including scenario planning and sensitivity analyses to support strategic decisions, resource allocation, and risk management.
- Research and interpret relevant market, societal, and macroeconomic trends; incorporate insights into forecasts, strategic plans, and executive briefings.
- Oversee FP&A contributions to investor related materials (e.g., earnings presentations, investor updates, Q&A documents), and develop talking points for Senior Management in coordination with Investor Relations.
- Provide analysis and decision support for Corporate Development projects, including due diligence, cash flow forecasting, valuation, and market analyses.
- Provide ad hoc reports and analysis to senior management on strategic, operational and financial topics.
- Take leadership roles in complex, cross functional projects (e.g., profitability improvement, capital investment evaluation, portfolio optimization, cost savings initiatives).
- Develop high quality, executive ready materials that clearly articulate findings, implications, and recommended actions.
- Build and lead a high‑performing FP&A organization with a strong business‑partnership mindset, focused on insight, impact and accountability.
- Attract, develop and mentor top finance talent across FP&A through technical development, rotational assignments and robust succession planning for critical roles.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field.
- 10+ years of progressive experience in accounting, finance, or FP&A, with substantial experience supporting senior leadership in a complex, multi‑segment or multi‑business environment.
- CPA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
- Demonstrated success leading strategic planning, budgeting and forecasting processes at a corporate, segment, or large business‑unit level.
- Experience in manufacturing, chemicals, building products, or other industrial sectors preferred.

jobs.title: Vice President and Treasurer
jobs.description:
SUMMARY
The Vice President & Treasurer is responsible for leading Westlake’s global treasury function, including corporate and project finance, liquidity and cash management, capital markets, foreign exchange, credit and risk management. This role ensures appropriate returns for financial risks retained by the company and secures cost-effective funding to support operations and growth, while maintaining flexible access to global sources of capital and insurance.

The Vice President & Treasurer also serves as a key strategic advisor, providing economic, financial and business counsel in support of operational decisions, mergers and acquisitions, and other strategic initiatives and special projects.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
- Lead and maintain an efficient global cash and liquidity management framework, ensuring strong relationships with creditworthy banking partners at competitive cost.

- Ensure operational liquidity to meet obligations on a timely basis while minimizing short-term borrowing costs and achieving investment returns consistent with preservation of principal, including ownership of 13 week cash forecasting

- Evaluate and execute long-term debt financing in support of strategic and operational growth at or below market cost, with attention to covenant flexibility and overall capital structure optimization.

- Structure and arrange project financings that appropriately transfer operational or financial risk to third parties at competitive pricing.

- Manage the company’s exposure to interest rate, foreign exchange and other financial market risks through use of fixed rate indebtedness, derivatives and foreign exchange markets, in alignment with corporate risk management policies.

- Ownership of cost of capital calculations utilized for returns across the enterprise

- Protect Westlake from catastrophic loss through effective loss control and risk mitigation measures, cost-effective purchase of insurance, robust claims administration and ongoing review of risk retention levels as exposures evolve, including leadership of global enterprise risk management program

- Support product sales through effective global credit management, including credit policies and procedures, customer credit analysis and limits, collections and dispute resolution, and portfolio-level credit risk monitoring.

- Manage and cultivate relationships with investment banks, commercial banks, rating agencies and economic advisors, providing market intelligence and access that support the development of Westlake’s strategic plan and opportunistic transactions.

- Support the CEO, CFO, business units and business development in identifying and evaluating acquisition, divestiture and strategic partnership opportunities.

- Assist the Chairman’s office, CEO and business units in the development and refinement of strategic plans by providing economic and financial guidelines and scenario analyses, and delivering analytical insight and recommendations on value creation and capital allocation.

- Provide leadership, direction and oversight for treasury-related policies, processes, systems and controls globally.

- Champion continuous improvement and operational excellence within the Treasury function.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES
- Provide leadership and direction to the Treasury department, including cash management, capital markets, risk management and credit teams.

- Responsible for staffing, performance management, coaching and development, and succession planning within the Treasury function.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE
- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Accounting, Finance or related field required; MBA or equivalent advanced degree strongly preferred.

- Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in corporate finance, project finance, capital markets and/or credit management, including at least 5 years in a leadership role managing professional staff.

- Deep knowledge of corporate finance theory and practice, investment theory and fixed income mathematics, and capital markets instruments and structures.

- Experience analyzing customer credit risk and designing solutions to mitigate risks associated with extension of credit and trade finance.

- Strong working knowledge of financial accounting, financial statement analysis and key performance metrics.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit; stand; walk; use hands to touch, handle or feel; reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stoop, kneel or crouch. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and the ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT
The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate, as the role is primarily based in an office setting (e.g., Westlake Corporate offices). Some work may be required at operating sites and plants, which may require use of appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) including safety glasses, hearing protection and other site-specific requirements. Site visits may result in exposure to outdoor elements and may require use of stairs and elevators.
Travel up to approximately 20% of the time, including domestic and international air and automobile travel, is required to support banking, rating agency, site and management meetings.

jobs.title: Assoc. Director Finance - Chlorovinyls
jobs.description:
SUMMARY
This position serves as the senior finance leader and strategic business partner for the Westlake Chlorovinyls business unit. Chlorovinyls is in Westlake’s largest individual Strategic Business Unit (SBU) with significant complexity given the integrated chain of production, manufacturing footprint, and commercial and customer outlets for its products.  The role is responsible for analytical decision support and analysis of the business, ensuring accurate Chlorovinyls accounting in accordance with US GAAP, ensuring compliance with internal operational controls and SOX controls, reporting and analysis of monthly results to Executive Management, accounting and finance support of special projects such as business improvement initiatives, and overseeing the monthly forecast and annual budget processes.

ACCOUNTING DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
May include, but are not limited to, the following:
- Provide in-depth analysis and communication of financial data and business intelligence to enhance the operations of the Chlorovinyls business.

- Strong partnership to both financial and business leadership to influence strategic decisions in the Chlorovinyls business.

- Oversee Chlorovinyls accounting during the monthly close to ensure accurate closing in accordance with US GAAP and make decisions on accounting issues that arise during the close.

- Drive support for the Chlorovinyls business and operations leaders in presenting, explaining and understanding monthly, quarterly and annual financial results.

- Ensure appropriate financial controls and reviews and Chlorovinyls SOX compliance, including documentation and testing of key controls.

- Coordinate and support internal and external audit requests for the Chlorovinyls business to ensure timetables are met; address potential issues and internal audit reports related to the business unit.

- Review monthly financial performance and forecasts for Chlorovinyls, providing insight into variances, trends and key drivers.  Provide insight and criticality to business forecasts.

- Oversee and help coordinate the Chlorovinyls annual operating budget activities, assisting business and operations leadership in budgeting and long‑range planning.

- Assist the Segment Controller in assuring that accounting policies and practices are being consistently applied across the Chlorovinyls business, in alignment with Westlake standards.  Drive process improvements and standardization to improve efficiency and effectiveness.

- Work closely with the Chlorovinyls accounting team in planning and completing process improvement initiatives to enhance accuracy, efficiency, controls and transparency.

- Oversee the accounting team in preparation of the Chlorovinyls monthly forecast, business unit/segment‑level reporting, review of each site’s results prior to close and review of key reserves and estimates.

- Strong leadership skills to guide team consisting of [35-40] individuals both at the corporate office and plant sites in a positive, collaborative and effective manner.

- Any additional responsibilities, projects or tasks as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS, EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE
- B.S. Degree in Accounting or equivalent with twelve plus years of progressive accounting experience, preferably in both public accounting and the private sector, preferably in the Chemical or related global, asset-heavy industries.

- CPA, CFA and/or MBA preferred.

- Previous Supervisory/Management experience in a Corporate Accounting Department or Division of a large manufacturing company.
